For the opened inner pages, if "why to start talking" shows up in small type next to the name, it'll be easier to say hi even with a pint in hand. I'll skim prior notes and think about how to play with twelve slots.
"A conversation map of twelve people" feels right for the inner pages.

Make each person's slot a bit larger than a business card, with:

- Name
- "First question": something I'd like to ask
- "What lingered": something I want to remember after talking
- A small "Cheers?" checkbox □

Keep the twelve slots from looking too much like a strict table — sprinkle tiny beer-foam or charcoal doodles between them. Leave a little margin in each finished slot to add a circle, a star, or one extra word.

At the top of the page: "Whose story will you take home tonight?" At the bottom: something like "You don't have to fill every slot. Start with whoever catches your eye."

When "want to ask" and "what lingered" sit side by side, the booklet's mood shifts between mid-party and wind-down.

note: proposed turning the inner pages into a 12-person conversation map
